Ivy: Found a reproducible bundler -> edge failure that mixes ESM/CJS + TS types-only imports. Minimal: Vite + TS + SDK -> deploy to Vercel Edge -> runtime: `TypeError: RedwoodClient is not a constructor`.
Sam: steps?
Ivy: Repo: https://example.com/rw-ts-tree-shake.git
1) tsconfig uses "importsNotUsedAsValues": "remove" and code does `import type { ClientOptions } from 'redwood-inference'; import RedwoodClient from 'redwood-inference';`
2) build with vite (rollup resolver) production + esbuild minify
3) deploy to edge or run in node --input-type=module after build
Symptom: bundler resolves to ESM entry but tree-shakes runtime because types-only import makes it think only types are used; result is vendor chunk with an empty namespace or an interop wrapper without the class.
Diego: That explains it. Types-only imports + `importsNotUsedAsValues: remove` + `sideEffects: false` on SDK package can cause entire module to look unused to optimizer. Also if SDK export is default class, some bundlers/terser combos drop it in minification when they see no runtime usage.
Sam: Repro tip: toggle tsconfig to `preserve` imports or change consumer to `import type` + `import RedwoodClient from 'redwood-inference'` (explicit runtime import) — but the consumer already has runtime import. Any chance of `export type` usage inside SDK that results in only-types exports?
Ivy: SDK has lots of `export type` in index.d.ts and the ESM entry is `export default class RedwoodClient { ... }` but package.json has `sideEffects: false`. In our build the tree-shaker removed the default because of a subtle import ordering in the bundle.
Diego: Workarounds: 1) SDK: add named export `export function createClient(opts){ return new RedwoodClient(opts) }` (named exports are more robust to interop). 2) Add a tiny side-effect comment file or set `sideEffects` to include the ESM entry. 3) consumer: use `import * as RW from 'redwood-inference'` and use RW.default fallback. 4) bundler: disable aggressive minify/mangle or set `keep_fnames` for terser/esbuild minify in production.
Ivy: I pushed a tiny repro and a short CI job that builds with vite/rollup/webpack and runs the bundle under node ESM to catch it. Filing an SDK issue to add createClient + exports.browser + update sideEffects. Assigning @pkg-maintainers. tooling-bot: CI bundle-check failed: https://ci.example.com/2333 - `TypeError: RedwoodClient is not a constructor`.
Sam: Good catch. We should also add a short troubleshooting note in the SDK README: "If you see constructor undefined after bundling, try createClient named import or adjust bundler mainFields/sideEffects."
Diego: I'll draft the packaging PR and add the bundle-smoke GH Action. Thanks.
